summary: This document registers the application/sql media type for the Structured Query Language (SQL). Registering it gives software a standard label for SQL content when it is sent or stored.

eli5.summary: This gives SQL, the language used to ask databases questions, an official name tag so computers know what kind of file they are holding.

questions: what is the media type for sql
subtitle: Standard media type label for SQL code and queries.

tldr.problem: SQL code needed an official media type label so software could properly identify and handle SQL content when sent over networks or stored in files.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6922 registers the media type application/sql with IANA, specifying how SQL should be labeled, including optional charset parameter and security considerations.
tldr.outcome: Applications can now consistently identify SQL content using the standard media type, improving interoperability across databases and tools.

today: RFC 6922 is an Informational RFC that registered the application/sql media type with IANA. It is now the standard label for SQL code and queries across databases, tools, and web applications.

sections.title: SQL Needs a Label
sections.content:
SQL (Structured Query Language) has been the standard language for working with databases for over 30 years. Programmers use it to create, read, and modify data. However, when SQL code is sent over the network or stored in a file, there was no standard way to label it as SQL.

Media types (also called MIME types) are labels that tell software what kind of content a file or transmission contains. For example, application/json means the content is JSON, and text/html means it is an HTML page. RFC 6922 registers a standard media type for SQL: application/sql.
sections.eli5: Before this, SQL code didn't have an official label. Now it does, so computers know when they are looking at a SQL file.

sections.title: Registration Details and Parameters
sections.content:
The RFC registers application/sql as the official media type. It defines an optional charset parameter that specifies the character encoding (like UTF-8 or ASCII) if needed. If no charset is specified, applications must not guess; they must inspect the content to detect the encoding.

One complication is that SQL itself may include character set information in the code. In those cases, the charset parameter should not be used to avoid conflicts.

SQL files are binary by nature and can contain database commands, queries, and potentially embedded code. This makes security important. Applications should only exchange SQL files with trusted parties and use security measures like virus scanning and restricted access. SQL files can expose sensitive information about database structure and contents, so encryption and protection against modification are important.
sections.eli5: The label includes options for saying what alphabet the code uses. SQL files can be dangerous because they control databases, so they need careful handling.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The RFC registers application/sql in the official IANA registry of media types. Since SQL implementations vary between different database vendors, users need to ensure that SQL files work with their specific database and version.
sections.eli5: The registration put SQL in the official list of media types. Now it is the standard name everyone uses.

references.text: Freed, N., Klensin, J., and T. Hansen, "Media Type Specifications and Registration Procedures", BCP 13, RFC 6838, January 2013.
